passages.text: WISCONSIN SOCIETY OF VETERINARY GRADUATES. <sentence_start/>The annual meeting was held in Madison, at the City Hall, Wednesday, February 5, 1896. <sentence_start/>The meeting was called to order by the President, Dr. J. P. Laws, at 1.45 p.m. <sentence_start/>The roll was then called, and the following mem- bers responded: W. G. Clark, J. R. Kelso, J. P. Laws, G. Ed. Leech, E. L. Morgenroth, E. H. Newton, C. H. Ormond, and J. F. Roub. <sentence_start/>Visitors: Drs. G. H. Fay, A. H. Hartwig, B. L. Clark, and Walter Pick. <sentence_start/>The minutes of the last meeting were read and approved. <sentence_start/>The President, in his report, gave a brief history of the Association from the time of organi- zation to the present date, which was interesting and instructive. <sentence_start/>The Secretary’s report of accounts was read and accepted. <sentence_start/>The Treasurer’s report was read and accepted. <sentence_start/>Dr. S. G. Binger, of Browntown, Green County, was expelled from the Association under charges preferred against him at the last annual meeting. <sentence_start/>Dr. Roub read a letter from Dr. Schmitt stating that he had fractured his hip, and could not be present. <sentence_start/>On motion, the sympathy of the Society was tendered Dr. Schmitt. <sentence_start/>Moved by Dr. Leech, and seconded by Dr. Roub, that a resolution of regret in regard to Dr. Brauchle's death be spread upon the minutes; carried. <sentence_start/>Applications for membership: Dr. G. H. Fay, Ripon, C.V.C., ’93; Dr. A. H. Hartwig, Watertown, C.V.C., ’95; Dr. B. L. Clarke, Monticello, C.V.C., ’95. <sentence_start/>A short recess was taken while the Censors considered the applications. <sentence_start/>The Censors reported favorably on the applications, and it was moved and seconded that they be elected to membership ; carried The Committee on Legislation reported in regard to the bill to regulate the practice of veterinary medicine and surgery which was before the Senate at the last session. <sentence_start/>The Committee was unable to bring sufficient influence to bear to secure the passage of the bill. <sentence_start/>On motion, the report was accepted and the Committee discharged. <sentence_start/>On motion, the Society proceeded to the election of officers for the en- suing year. <sentence_start/>The following gentlemen were elected : Dr. G. Ed. <sentence_start/>Leech Milwaukee, President; Dr. C. H. Ormond, Milwaukee, Vice-President; Dr. W. G. Clark, Beaver Dam, Secretary ; Dr. J. P. Laws, Madison, Treasurer; Drs. A. H. Hartwig, Watertown ; B. L. Clark, Monticello; and E. H. New- ton, Waupun, Censors. <sentence_start/>Moved by Dr. Leech, and seconded by Dr. Kelso, that the Society revert to new business; carried. <sentence_start/>On motion, the Secretary was instructed to inform the Society of those who have been elected members of the Society and have not qualified. <sentence_start/>The following names were read and voted upon separately, and dropped from the roll of the Society YDrs. <sentence_start/>F. E. Stone, S. W. Mount, J. L. Kearney, and I. Philip. <sentence_start/>Moved and seconded, that U. S. Inspectors of the Bureau of Animal Industry be invited to attend and take part in the Association meetings. <sentence_start/>On motion, the Society adjourned until 7.30 p.m. <sentence_start/>Evening Session. <sentence_start/>Meeting called to order by the President at 7.30 o’clock. <sentence_start/>The question of legislation was discussed, and it was decided to appoint a committee to draft a bill and present it before the Society at the semi- annual meeting. <sentence_start/>Drs. <sentence_start/>Leech, Clark, and Law were appointed as a Com- mittee on Legislation. <sentence_start/>On motion, the subject of army veterinary legislation was referred to the Committee on Legislation. <sentence_start/>Dr. Leech introduced a resolution requesting that the Association adopt, at its next meeting, as a part of its Code of Ethics, the following : " It shall be deemed a violation of the Code of Ethics for any member of this Asso- ciation to contract with or through the officers of any live-stock insurance company for the professional treatment of the members’ stock so insured; but this rule shall not prevent any member from becoming the examiner of risks, and to act in the capacity of expert for the same. <sentence_start/>On motion, this was laid over until the next meeting. <sentence_start/>Reading of essays: “ Shoeing,” Dr. E. L. Morgenroth; “ Scientific Breeding,” Dr. J. R. Kelso; “Equine Relapsing-fever,” Dr. T. W. Wat- son ; “Veterinary Meat-inspection by the State, and its Necessity,” Dr. G. Ed..<sentence_start/>Leech; “Professional Ethics,” Dr. J. P. Laws. <sentence_start/>The essays were well prepared, and brought out an interesting discussion. <sentence_start/>Dr. Watson was unable to attend, and his essay was read by the Secretary. <sentence_start/>On motion, it was decided to hold the semi-annual meeting at Milwaukee, subject to the call of the Secretary. <sentence_start/>Moved and seconded, that the balance of the special assessment remain- ing unpaid be remitted. <sentence_start/>Adjournment. <sentence_start/>W. G. <sentence_start/>Clark, M.D.C., Secretary.
